jobs.occupation: Postdoc in the Strep A Vaccine Research Group at the NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious postdoctoral fellow who has experience in protein biochemistry, enzymology, recombinant protein expression, and functional assay development.

  The position is initially available for 24 months. An extension may be possible subject to project progress, funding and mutual agreement. The position is expected to commence on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, as agreed with the successful candidate.

  The fellow will join the Strep A Vaccine Research Group led by A/Prof Stephan Brouwer at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI) Research Center, which is embedded in the Department of Immunology and Microbiology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

  Background

  The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

   	
• NIVI Research Center (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology. 	
• NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.   NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Our research

  Our group is part of the NIVI-R interdisciplinary research consortium and focuses on the discovery, characterization, and evaluation of vaccine antigens from Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus; Strep A). Strep A is responsible for a substantial global burden of disease, ranging from pharyngitis and skin infections to life-threatening invasive disease and post-infectious autoimmune complications. Despite decades of research, no licensed vaccine is currently available.

  Our research aims to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying Strep A pathogenesis and protective immunity, and to translate this knowledge into the development of next-generation vaccines. We combine bacterial genetics, molecular microbiology, biochemistry, protein science, functional immunology, human cellular models, and pre-clinical infection models to identify and evaluate vaccine antigens and immune correlates of protection.

  A major focus of the group is the development of functional assays to characterize Strep A virulence factors and vaccine antigens. These assays are used to define biological function, investigate host-pathogen interactions, evaluate antibody-mediated neutralization, and establish mechanistic links between antigen-specific immune responses and protection.

  We are a young, international, and collaborative team that values scientific rigor, creativity, mentorship, and teamwork. As part of NIVI, we work closely with leading groups in airway immunity, vaccine formulation and adjuvants, structural biology, and we benefit from close ties to Statens Serum Institut and to NIVI-D’s translational pipeline. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive research environment and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds; we value diversity across gender, nationality, career stage, and scientific training.

  Your job

  We strive to build a cohesive research environment in which individual projects contribute to a shared goal: developing and validating vaccine antigens that can advance Strep A vaccine development. As our new postdoctoral fellow, you will lead the development and implementation of functional assays for the characterization of Strep A antigens and virulence factors.

  Your primary responsibilities will include designing, developing, optimizing, and validating biochemical, enzymatic, cellular, and immunological assays to investigate antigen function and assess vaccine-induced antibody responses. You will contribute to recombinant protein production and characterization, establish functional readouts for antigen activity, and develop assays suitable for evaluating antibody-mediated inhibition or neutralization of virulence-associated mechanisms.

  The project will involve extensive laboratory work encompassing molecular cloning, recombinant protein expression, protein purification, protein characterization, enzymology, and cell-based assays. In addition, you will contribute to the development of opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays and other functional immune assays using relevant human cell culture systems.

  You will be expected to independently drive your research project with a high degree of scientific autonomy while actively collaborating with colleagues within the group and the broader NIVI consortium. Responsibilities will also include data analysis, manuscript preparation, presentation of results at group and consortium meetings, and dissemination of findings at international conferences. The successful candidate will benefit from regular mentoring and career-development discussions tailored to their professional goals.

  The project will include the following key areas:

   	
• Development and validation of biochemical and enzymatic assays to characterize Strep A vaccine antigens and virulence-associated proteins. 	
• Recombinant expression, purification, and biophysical characterization of bacterial proteins required for functional assay development. 	
• Development of antibody-functional assays, including neutralization, inhibition, and mechanism-of-action studies. 	
• Establishment and optimization of opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays and other cellular assays relevant to vaccine-induced protection. 	
• Investigation of host-pathogen interactions using mammalian cell culture systems and functional immunological assays.   While the precise experimental emphasis may evolve as the project progresses, the successful candidate is expected to contribute across these interconnected areas, with a primary focus on establishing robust functional assays that support antigen discovery, characterization, and vaccine evaluation.

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and creative scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• You have a PhD in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Immunology, or a closely related field. 	
• You have significant hands-on experience developing, optimizing, and troubleshooting biochemical, enzymatic, or protein-based functional assays. 	
• You have strong expertise in recombinant protein expression, purification, and characterization. 	
• You possess a solid understanding of protein biochemistry, enzyme kinetics, protein-protein interactions, and structure-function relationships. 	
• You have experience with molecular cloning and standard molecular biology techniques. 	
• You have experience working with mammalian cell culture systems. 	
• You have demonstrated ability to independently design experiments and solve complex technical challenges. 	
• You have a strong record of scientific productivity, as demonstrated by peer-reviewed publications and other scientific achievements. 	
• You are collaborative, communicative, and enjoy working in an interdisciplinary team environment. 	
• You have excellent English communication skills, both written and spoken. 	
• You are motivated to develop new methods and expand your scientific expertise.   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience with bacterial pathogens and host-pathogen interaction research. 	
• Experience developing antibody-functional assays, including neutralization, inhibition, or immune-effector assays. 	
• Experience with opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays or related phagocyte-based functional assays. 	
• Experience with primary immune cells, macrophage cell lines, neutrophil-like cell lines, or other relevant cellular models. 	
• Experience with biophysical protein characterization techniques, such as SPR, SEC-MALS, CD spectroscopy, or related methods. 	
• Experience with protein structural analysis or structure-guided antigen characterization.   Overall, it is expected that you contribute actively to a positive, collaborative and productive work environment. A strong scientific track record with a productive publication list will also weigh strongly in the assessment.

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include state-of-the-art laboratories for molecular microbiology, protein biochemistry, and assay development, together with BSL-2 containment facilities for work with bacterial pathogens. We have extensive infrastructure for recombinant protein expression, purification, and characterization, including SPR-based interaction analysis and other biophysical characterization platforms. Dedicated mammalian cell culture facilities support the development of host-pathogen interaction and opsonophagocytic killing assays, while advanced microscopy facilities enable cellular and mechanistic studies. Researchers additionally have access to UCPH core facilities for genomics, proteomics, flow cytometry, and bioinformatics.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position initially limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07% to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for favourable taxation under the Danish researcher taxation scheme, subject to applicable rules and individual eligibility.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities applicable at the time of appointment.

  Questions

  For further information on the position, please contact Stephan Brouwer (stephan.brouwer@sund.ku.dk), or for administrative questions P&O Hannah Margrethe Borg Sortland (hannah.sortland@sund.ku.dk)

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure

  Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications. 	
• List of up to 3 references and their contact information.   Deadline for applications: 1st of November, 23.59 CET

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline and not to consider applications that do not meet the requirements.

  The further process

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Interviews are expected to be held in weeks 48-49.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

You will translate demand into supply: what to buy, how much, and when. Your decisions will directly affect product availability for our customers and the cash commitment to inventory. The Cosmic Dawn Center (DAWN) invites applications for both the DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowship and postdoctoral positions to work on specific projects.

In addition, DAWN has several associates at major research institutes across Europe, North America, and Australia.   DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended for outstanding scientists whose research falls within DAWN’s research themes focused on the early Universe: first stars, high-redshift galaxy evolution, reionization and evolution of the IGM, high-redshift transients and supernovae, dust and ISM in the early Universe, massive galaxy evolution, and dark matter. DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to pursue their own independent, cutting-edge research programs in collaboration with DAWN members.

  Postdoctoral positions

  Up to two postdoctoral position are available as part of the DFF Sapere Aude-funded project “Revealing Massive Stars at Cosmic Dawn” in Associate Professor Charlotte Mason’s group at DAWN/NBI to work on both observational and theoretical projects on galaxy formation and reionization, with a particular focus on JWST spectroscopy from the SPURS survey. Applicants with interests and expertise in any of galaxy formation, stellar populations, Lyman-alpha emission, IGM/CGM evolution, galaxy-dark matter connections at high redshift, JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy, statistical inference and comparing hydrodynamical simulations to observations are strongly encouraged to apply.

More information on DAWN’s activities and researchers is available at https://cosmicdawn.dk.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in Economics at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one fully funded PhD scholarship at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark. The position is based at SDU’s Esbjerg campus.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the 5+3 PhD programme. The programme includes a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offers a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January 2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within five research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; Microeconomics; and Environmental and Resource Economics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Environmental and Resource Economics (ERE) group, which focuses on Environmental and Natural resource economics on a variety of topics, namely ecosystem conservation and use, marine resource use, management and conservation, energy transitions, climate regulation, and interdisciplinary research at the interface between economics and the natural sciences. The group applies economic theory and tools to policy and analysis to provide guidance for more efficient use of environmental and natural resource goods and services.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professors Ana Faria Lopes and Melina Kourantidou.  Part of the work will contribute to the BRAVE (Biological Invasions Resolved through Adaptable, Versatile, and Engaging Nature-Based Solutions) project, a Biodiversa+ -funded project that investigates the complex ecological and societal challenges associated with invasive species and their management. In particular, the research will contribute to the Danish BRAVE case study on the invasive Pacific oyster in the Wadden Sea, including work on stakeholder preferences, economic values, and trade-offs associated with its management. For further information about the project, please see this link or this link.

The project relies on the application of economic theories, namely non-market valuation and bioeconomic modelling, to investigate the management of invasive species. We welcome candidates with strong quantitative and analytical skills from economics or related disciplines, including candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds and an interest in environmental and resource management.  There will be considerable scope for the PhD student to develop their own research questions within the broader themes of the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, through both collaborative research and independent work, including a single-authored paper. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Ana Faria Lopes as the main supervisor and will join a research group that includes postdoctoral researcher and research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Environmental and Resource Management, Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in data analysis and applied quantitative methods using R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have willingness to participate in stakeholder engagement activities and communicate research findings to different audiences. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, non-market valuation, press analysis, GIS and/or bioeconomic modelling.

• 
Experience conducting empirical research.

• 
Demonstrated interest in environmental and resource economics.

• 
Knowledge of Danish or another Scandinavian language would be an advantage for stakeholder engagement and work with locally relevant material but is not a requirement.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used.

SDU Robotics currently has an open 2-year postdoc position in relation to CAPeX; specifically, for the development of a robotic solution for automation of laboratory experiments that require manipulation of tubes, fragile glass vials, and liquids. The robotic solution should be flexible in the sense that it should be able to conduct several experiments with little user-intervention, operate alongside humans, and recover from failures. Consequently, visual feedback must be used for adapting robot behavior to a dynamic environment.  The postdoc should contribute to the deployment of the developed solution in laboratories in both SDU and DTU. The successful candidate will work closely with other PhDs and postdoc candidates in CAPeX.

As a postdoctoral researcher, your role will encompass mainly research, but teaching responsibilities could also be part of the employment. The main duties and responsibilities include: 

• 
Research in collaboration with colleagues from SDU Robotics and CAPeX.

• 
Conducting scientific research and publishing the results in high quality scientific conferences/journals.

• 
Supporting the team in securing external funding.

• 
Contributing to the project CAPeX deliverables. 

 

Profile and requirements

The position requires research experience at PhD level in a relevant area such as robotics, preferably applied to robotic systems controlled using visual feedback. The candidate is hence expected to have most of the following qualifications:

• 
Expert knowledge in the control of robots

• 
Experience in simulation of robotic systems

• 
Experience in design and development of robotic systems

• 
Experience with using computer vision.

•

• 
Have a strong sense of responsibility.

Conduct independent research.

The candidate will be integrated into the SDU Robotics unit, which is a team of approx. 60 employees. We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team with flexible work organization and support for individual development.

SDU Robotics is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and located at the main Campus in Odense, at the core of the Odense Robotics Cluster involving 120+ startups and established companies in robotics. The group is involved in a variety of national and European projects and features a strong network of academic and industrial partners.

We are a team specialized in robot solutions involving modelling, estimation, and control of advanced robot systems. In addition, the candidate will be integrated into CAPeX - a pioneer center for accelerating P2X materials discovery and working on automation of laboratory experiments.

CAPeX is a 13-year and 300 MDKK “Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery”, funded by Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, the Danish National Research Foundation, the Carlsberg Foundation, the Lundbeck Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and the Villum Foundation. CAPeX is hosted by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and co-hosted by Aalborg University (AAU), and unites leading experts from DTU, AAU, University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, and the University of Southern Denmark with international partners from Stanford University, Utrecht University, and the University of Toronto to form a truly Pioneering Center on P2X. You can read more about the CAPeX research themes and X-trails, our organization, and the other open PhD and postdoc cohort positions at http://www.capex-p2x.com. 

We look forward to receiving your application and to supporting your academic growth as a researcher in SDU Robotics.
